extracted.intended_audience: American statesmen, diplomats, correspondents, and a young student (Peter Carr)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Thomas Jefferson's letters offering prescriptive guidance on federal government structure, diplomacy, commerce, and a detailed recommended curriculum and method for a young student's education and moral/religious inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal division: one for foreign, several for domestic
rubrics_metrics.description: My general plan would be, to make the States one as to every thing connected with foreign nations, and several as to every thing purely domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate a federal government unified in external relations and fragmented for internal/domestic matters. This supports coherent foreign policy while preserving state autonomy for internal affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of executive and legislative powers in Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: I think it very material, to separate, in the hands of Congress, the executive and legislative powers, as the judiciary already are, in some degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jefferson argues that executive details in a legislative assembly are the source of much inefficiency and mischief, occupying the body with small execution tasks that displace important legislation; if the convention does not recommend it, Congress should establish an executive committee itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied power of compulsion to enforce compacts
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been so often said, as to be generally believed, that Congress have no power by the Confederation to enforce any thing; for example, contributions of money. It was not necessary to give them that power expressly; they have it by the law of nature. When two parties make a compact, there results to each a power of compelling the other to execute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use natural-law reasoning to justify federal enforcement of agreements (e.g., using naval force to levy on commerce) and trust Congress to exercise such powers sparingly and only at last extremity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal commerce powers need improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: But with all the imperfections of our present government, it is, without comparison, the best existing... Its greatest defect is the imperfect manner in which matters of commerce have been provided for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize commerce regulation and enforcement as a principal defect to be remedied in constitutional reform; legislative design should more effectively provide for commercial matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid legislatures handling execution details
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is so embarrassing nor so mischievous, in a great assembly, as the details of execution. The smallest trifle of that kind, occupies as long as the most important act of legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should remove executional minutiae from large legislative bodies to preserve attention for major legislative acts; create separate executive structures or committees for execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing political/commercial initiatives to local conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Since writing thus far, I have received an intimation, that it will be agreeable not to press our commercial regulations at this moment, the ministry being too much occupied with the difficulties surrounding them, to spare a moment on any subject which will admit of delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not press diplomatic or commercial negotiations when the foreign government is preoccupied or in crisis; waiting may avoid defeat of the objective and be politically prudent.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an envoy may act without prior orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters, arising within the kingdom of France, to which my commission is limited, and not admitting time to take the orders of Congress, I suppose I may move in originally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diplomatic agents should refer to central government when practicable, but where time is short and matters fall within their limited commission, they may act originally; for matters where parties are within reach of Congress, direct application to Congress is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular and commercial complaints should be routed through Congress where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever parties are within the reach of Congress, they should apply to them, and my instructions come through that channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the central government's primacy in handling claims and commercial complaints when Congress can be reached; only intervene locally when immediacy or commission limits require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use payment to quiet foreign officers and preserve influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Above all things, it is desirable to hush the foreign officers by payment. Their wants, the nature of their services, their access to high characters, and connections with them, bespeak the reasons for this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment to foreign officers both compensates services and stabilizes diplomatic relations; financial settlement can materially improve a nation's standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate filiation of Indian nations by languages
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an object I mean to pursue, as I am persuaded that the only method of investigating the filiation of the Indian nations, is by that of their languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect vocabularies and pursue comparative linguistic work as the primary method for tracing relationships among indigenous nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess navigational inventions by two technical criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply this table to use in the voyage between America and Europe, suppose the variation to increase a degree in every one hundred and sixty miles. Two difficulties occur; 1. a ready and accurate method of finding the variation of the place; 2. an instrument so perfect, as that (though the degree on it shall represent one hundred and sixty miles) it shall give the parts of the degree so minutely, as to answer the purpose of the navigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility of a navigational variation table depends on (1) a reliable method to determine local magnetic variation and (2) sufficiently precise instruments to resolve small parts of a degree for practical navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government non-intervention in inventions as public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Their policy is to leave their citizens free, neither restraining nor aiding them in their pursuits... though the interposition of government in matters of invention has its use, yet it is in practice so inseparable from abuse, that they think it better not to meddle with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer laissez-faire toward inventions at the policy level to avoid abuses of governmental intervention; rely on private or foreign governments to reward useful discoveries when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language learning order and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: 1. Italian. I fear the learning this language will confound your French and Spanish... 2. Spanish. Bestow great attention on this, and endeavor to acquire an accurate knowledge of it. Our future connections with Spain and Spanish America, will render that language a valuable acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize Spanish study over Italian for practical utility and to avoid confusing Romance languages; acquire accurate knowledge (Jefferson even sends a dictionary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral philosophy learned by practice, not lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: I think it lost time to attend lectures on this branch... The moral sense, or conscience, is as much a part of man, as his leg or arm... This sense may be strengthened by exercise... read good books, because they will encourage, as well as direct your feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overreliance on formal lectures for moral education; instead read morally edifying literature (Sterne recommended), and exercise virtues (gratitude, generosity, charity, truth, justice, firmness, order, courage) to strengthen conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reason and impartial inquiry in religious examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Divest yourself of all bias in favor of novelty and singularity of opinion... Fix reason firmly in her seat, and call to her tribunal every fact, every opinion. Question with boldness even the existence of a God... Read the Bible... examine with more care those facts which contradict the laws of nature... examine upon what evidence [inspiration] is founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach religious texts with impartiality and critical reasoning: compare testimony against natural laws and probabilities, read both canonical and pseudo-evangelists, and weigh the evidence for extraordinary claims rather than accepting them on authority or fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read broadly and judge claims yourself rather than deferring to ecclesiastical authority
rubrics_metrics.description: You should read all the histories of Christ, as well of those whom a council of ecclesiastics have decided for us to be Pseudo-evangelists, as those they named Evangelists. Because these Pseudo-evangelists pretended to inspiration as much as the others, and you are to judge their pretensions by your own reason, and not by the reason of those ecclesiastics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include disputed sources in study because their claims to inspiration merit individual examination; do not accept ecclesiastical verdicts as a substitute for personal reasoned judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical consolation through activity after loss
rubrics_metrics.description: It is better to turn from the contemplation of our misfortunes, to the resources we possess for extricating ourselves... the very activity necessary for this, is a state of greater happiness than the unoccupied one, to which you had a thought of retiring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recovering from significant losses, favor active engagement in recovery efforts and employ one's talents and habits of business rather than withdrawing into retirement; activity is both a means to recovery and a source of greater happiness.
